devon: starting a sparrow-lite int4 canary run to repro structured-output parse spikes. seeing streaming responses where tool_call array fragments end up with stray delimiters between chunks. paste of raw stream fragments below for context.

devon: ```
--chunk A--
{"output":[{"tool_call":{"name":"search","arguments":"{\"q\":\"widget\",\"page\":1}"}}
--chunk B--
, {"tool_call":{"name":"summarize","arguments":"{\"len\":\"short\"}"}}]
--assembled--
{"output":[{"tool_call":{"name":"search","arguments":"{\"q\":\"widget\",\"page\":1}"}},{"tool_call":{"name":"summarize","arguments":"{\"len\":\"short\"}"}}]}
```

devon: chunk B begins with a comma and later closes the array; naive stitcher concatenates and occasionally injects an extra comma -> host-side JSON.parse fails. this only shows up on int4 canary with streaming + kv-cache + microbatch>1. non-streaming is fine. parse_fail_rate jumped from ~0.5% -> 3.4% after enabling int4 microbatching.

ops-bot: canary:job="sparrow-lite-int4-2026-03-22" parse_fail=0.034 rps=610 p50_ms=88

linh: curious if tokenizer splitting multibyte sequences across frames is causing a dangling escape or comma. can you dump token boundaries for the failing traces?

devon: token snapshot: mostly ASCII, split boundaries at token idxs chunkA [0..19], chunkB [20..35]. nothing obvious, but we do see the emitted raw bytes sometimes end with '}]' and chunkB starts with ', {'.

sara: is the runtime or the downstream stitcher adding commas? mike, we discussed stitcher behavior last year.

mike: runtime forwards framed fragments; stitcher currently does a simple join of array fragments separated by ',' when reassembling. bug: it doesn't check if fragments already include opening/closing brackets. I'll prepare a stitcher patch to trim leading/trailing commas/brackets and to optionally enable NDJSON streaming mode.

ana: mitigation suggestions: 1) opt-in NDJSON: emit one top-level object per line for toolcalls; 2) sentinel framing like <TOOL_END> between tool_call items; 3) temporary parse-retry backoff increase. NDJSON lowest-risk.

devon: I ran a quick mitigation: flush prefix cache at tool_call boundaries for the canary for 3 hours. parse_fail went down to 0.2% during that window but p50 increased ~6ms.

ops-bot: canary:job="sparrow-lite-int4-2026-03-22-flush" parse_fail=0.002 p50_ms=94 rps=605

linh: please add a regression test that simulates mid-json chunk splits and stitch behavior. I couldn't reproduce locally until I used the same microbatch distribution and random split seed.

devon: eval_id=eval-2026-03-22-9001. sample generator (pseudo):
```python
def split_stream(s, maxlen=50):
    i=0
    while i<len(s):
        cut = min(len(s), i + random.randint(8, maxlen))
        yield s[i:cut]
        i = cut
```

devon: next steps: mike to open PR for stitcher hardening + NDJSON opt-in header, sara to add metric toolcall_fragmentation_count and a unit/integration test, linh to confirm tokenizer edgecases, I'll keep the flush mitigation active until runtime fix lands. target rollout: canary patch -> 20% in 12h if parse_fail <0.5% and p50 latency regression <10ms.

mike: on it. will post PR and link here. plan to include: defensive stitching (trim punctuation), NDJSON header, and an opt-in flag for legacy clients.

sara: I'll add the metric dashboards and alert on >1% parse_fail for the canary. also add an e2e that streams with intentional boundary commas.

ana: agreed. NDJSON seems the least invasive long-term fix; sentinel framing is heavier.

devon: thanks team. assigning follow-ups in the ticket. will update this thread with PR and canary numbers.
